title: Compatibility shim layer patterns + changelog synthesis for v1->v2 SDK transition
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a pragmatic compatibility shim pattern and automated changelog synthesis process to smooth developer migration from SDK v1 -> v2 across Python, TypeScript, and Go. This ticket covers: 1) design and implementation of lightweight adapter/shim libraries that allow common v1 callsites to work with v2 runtime semantics; 2) an automated pipeline that synthesizes release notes and changelog entries from codemods, PR labels, and annotated migration guides; 3) examples and cookbook entries showing retry semantics and streaming ergonomics adapters per language.
background: Several teams have reported substantial friction upgrading from v1 to v2 due to: renamed client constructors, changed retry semantics (sync->async backoff behavior), and new streaming APIs that expose chunked events instead of final result callbacks. Existing docs (PRDs and playbooks) cover the surface area but do not provide a low-friction compatibility path. We previously prototyped codemods and CLI helpers (ENG-20527), and this ticket formalizes a library pattern plus changelog automation to reduce manual work for releases.
acceptance_criteria: Provide three small language-specific shim packages (py-redwood-compat, @redwood/compat, redwood-compat-go) that enable the top 5 most common v1 call patterns to operate unchanged in v2 builds
Documented adapter recipes for: retry semantics normalization, streaming->callback adapter, and streaming->iterator adapter for each language
A GitHub Action that generates a draft CHANGELOG.md section per release by aggregating codemod output, PR labels (migration, breaking-change, docs), and a manually curated 'migration-notes.md' file
End-to-end example repos (one per language) that demonstrate migrating a small app with minimal changes using the shims
Automated tests for each shim that run in CI and assert parity on 10 canonical v1->v2 behavioral cases (retries, timeouts, stream ordering)
implementation_notes: Shim design principle: small surface, shallow indirection. Export the v1 function names that internally map to v2 client calls with explicit opt-in for new features
Example Python shim entrypoint: class RedwoodClientCompat: def generate(self, *args, **kwargs): -> translates to v2 'responses.stream' or 'responses.create' based on 'stream' kwarg
TS shim should expose both callback-based and async-iterable adapters. Provide function 'fromV1Calls(clientV2, opts) -> legacyAPI' returning a thin object with legacy method names
Go shim will use interface types to accept both blocking and streaming styles. Provide helpers: StreamToChannel(ctx, stream) and ChannelToSync(ctx, ch) to help consumers gradually migrate
Retry normalization: create 'compat_retry' helpers that implement v1 backoff constants and jitter behavior mapped onto v2 retry hooks. Expose a compatibility flag 'legacy_backoff=true'
Streaming ergonomics adapters: implement 'stream_to_callback' and 'stream_to_iterator' in each shim. When using v2 streaming, buffer metadata and deliver events with a compatible framing format

Changelog synthesis: pipeline reads codemod output (jsonl) from ./codemods/output/, merges with PR labels using GitHub GraphQL to fetch PR titles and authors, then emits markdown chunks following our release template
Provide an opt-out mechanism: shims must be published under a separate package name and not be the default import to avoid long-term maintenance burden
risks: Shims mask breaking changes which may slow adoption of v2 idioms
Maintenance overhead: keeping shims in sync with future v2 feature changes
Automated changelog synthesis may produce noisy entries if codemods are imprecise; requires human review step
Edge cases in streaming ordering semantics (partial tokens vs framed events) could cause subtle application-level regressions
qa_plan: Unit tests for each shim function with deterministically mocked v2 runtime
Integration tests that run the example repos against a local v2 dev server (fixture) validating request/response parity
Performance test: ensure shim overhead adds <5ms median latency for common fast-path calls and does not increase p95 by >10%
Manual migration test: run a small customer sample migration checklist and capture developer feedback
Changelog pipeline test: run the GH Action in dry-run mode and verify generated markdown meets editorial guidelines
